recipes.name: Chinese Tomato Egg Stir-fry
recipes.description: This 10-minute Chinese tomato egg stir-fry is a dish you’ll find on many Chinese home dinner tables. It’s fast, easy, cheap, and delicious. And vegetarian!

video.name: Tomato-Egg-stir-fry_AdT.mp4
video.description: Sarah shows you how to whip up Chinese Tomato and Egg Stir-fry, a home cooking staple in any Chinese household!

recipeIngredient: 4  small to medium tomatoes ((about 500 g, 1 pound))

recipeInstructions.text: Start by cutting tomatoes into small wedges and finely chop the scallion.
recipeInstructions.name: Start by cutting tomatoes into small wedges and finely chop the scallion.

recipeInstructions.text: Crack 4 eggs into a bowl and season with ¼ teaspoon salt, ¼ teaspoon white pepper, ½ teaspoon sesame oil, and 1 teaspoon Shaoxing wine. Beat eggs for a minute.
recipeInstructions.name: Crack 4 eggs into a bowl and season with ¼ teaspoon salt, ¼ teaspoon white pepper, ½ teaspoon sesame oil, and 1 teaspoon Shaoxing wine. Beat eggs for a minute.

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the wok over medium heat until it just starts to smoke. Then add 2 tablespoons of oil and immediately add the eggs. Scramble the eggs and remove from the wok immediately. Set aside.
recipeInstructions.name: Preheat the wok over medium heat until it just starts to smoke. Then add 2 tablespoons of oil and immediately add the eggs. Scramble the eggs and remove from the wok immediately. Set aside.

recipeInstructions.text: Add 1 more tablespoon oil to the wok, turn up the heat to high, and add the tomatoes and scallions. Stir-fry for 1 minute, and then add 2 teaspoons sugar, ½ teaspoon salt, and ¼ cup water (if your stove gets very hot and liquid tends to cook off very quickly in your wok, add a little more water). Add the cooked eggs.
recipeInstructions.name: Add 1 more tablespoon oil to the wok, turn up the heat to high, and add the tomatoes and scallions. Stir-fry for 1 minute, and then add 2 teaspoons sugar, ½ teaspoon salt, and ¼ cup water (if your stove gets very hot and liquid tends to cook off very quickly in your wok, add a little more water). Add the cooked eggs.

recipeInstructions.text: Mix everything together, cover the wok, and cook for 1-2 minutes, until the tomatoes are completely softened.

recipeInstructions.text: Uncover, and continue to stir-fry over high heat until the sauce thickens to your liking. Serve!

recipes.description: Braised Chinese Mushrooms with Bok Choy is a delicious dish that’s just a little bit fancy, made with baby bok choy and fragrant braised dried Chinese mushrooms. Makes for a great side dish or a main for vegans seeking meaty mushroom goodness!

recipeInstructions.text: Place the dried Chinese mushrooms into a medium bowl, and pour 2-3 cups of hot water over them. Place a plate over the bowl so the mushrooms are completely submerged. Because the mushrooms are small, they should reconstitute quickly. After 15 minutes, cut off the stems of the mushrooms and return them to the water to soak for another 15 minutes.

recipes.description: This Smashed Asian cucumber salad recipe is light, refreshing and perfect for the summer, but packed with flavor from a zingy dressing, garlic, and cilantro. It only takes 10 minutes to make!

video.name: Smashed Cucumber Salad
video.description: Smashed Asian Cucumber Salad is the easiest summer dish. It's garlicky, refreshing and also a little spicy! Add your favorite chili oil and watch it disappear!

recipes.name: Chicken and Mushroom Clay Pot Rice
recipes.description: A Chinese home-cooked comfort food recipe with mushrooms, wood ears, lily flowers, and the silkiest chicken!
recipeIngredient: 6  dried shiitake mushrooms ((small to medium size))
8 ounces boneless skinless chicken thighs ((or 6 chicken drumettes and wingettes/flats))
1 cup low sodium chicken stock ((or water))
1  scallion ((finely chopped; green parts and white parts separated))

recipeInstructions.text: Add the dried mushrooms, dried lily flowers, and dried wood ears to 3 separate bowls. video.description: Sichuan Boiled Pork, a signature dish of Sichuan cuisine, holds simple yet irresistible flavors in its numbing and spicy broth.

recipeIngredient: 30ml cooking oil (for enhancing the aroma at the end)

recipeInstructions.text: First, cut 350g of pork loin into thin slices as evenly as possible and put them into a bowl.
Then, add 1 egg white, 4g of salt, 5ml of light soy sauce, 5ml of cooking wine and 10g of cornstarch. Mix well and marinate for 5 minutes to let the slices absorb the flavors.
While marinating the meat, prepare the side ingredients: Trim and wash 500g of bean sprouts, chop 20g of scallions and mince 20g of garlic for standby.
After 5 minutes of marination, heat the pan, add 20ml of oil and put the bean sprouts into the pan. Stir - fry them quickly for several times.
Then, sprinkle 2g of salt and stir - fry evenly until the bean sprouts become a little soft. Transfer them to a plate for standby.

Add more oil to the pan, put in 50g of doubanjiang and stir - fry slowly over low heat until it becomes loose. After getting the red oil, add 300ml of water, stir well, then add 5g of salt. Bring it to a boil over high heat to make a red and spicy soup in the pan.

When the water is boiling, carefully put the marinated slices into the pan and stir gently. Once the slices change from red to white, which means they are cooked. As soon as the soup boils again, immediately scoop out the soup and the slices together and pour them over the bean sprouts.
Sprinkle 10g of chili powder and 10g of Sichuan pepper powder over the slices and bean sprouts, then evenly distribute the chopped scallions and minced garlic on top.
Finally, heat 30ml of oil until boiling hot (smoky).
Pour the hot oil directly over the chopped scallions and minced garlic. Thus, the Sichuan Boiled Pork is completed.

I have a bit of advice for you folks that I'm quite certain your many readers will find not just useful, but lifesaving. If I recommended a wine, I had to be darn sure, beforehand, that there was an adequate supply in town to handle a big demand--otherwise I'd have a whole lot of unhappy readers, not to mention vendors. I suggest you might think along the same lines.
For example, in this recipe, you recommend TanTan Xian Hunan Salted Chilis. That's fine...except: most of us Out Here are going to have to go online to find this condiment, to Amazon, to Weee, to Yami, etc. But guess what? None of these folks have it, either they never did, or it's all sold out. There are two obscure vendors online who *do* have it: one, for $15+shipping; the other for c. $3+$21 shipping. In other words, none of us is going to find TanTan chilies anywhere, unless we live somewhere with a great Asian market, which most of us don't.
Let me suggest then, that when you recommend some very special product, such as Tan Tan, which might be very hard for us out here to find, that you also recommend something additional, something widely available either online or in a well-equipped supermarket in, say, Albany, or Ft. Collins. For example, if Dynasty or Lee Kum Kee makes something close enough--maybe not as great as Tan Tan but workable nonetheless--you could tell us that it would work as Plan B. recipes.description: 到合肥十年了 这道久负盛名的徽州名菜 一直不敢吃 怕吃不惯特殊的臭味 直到今年元旦到西递宏村玩的时候 想着既然都来到了古徽州 那一定是要尝一下臭鳜鱼的 不管喜不喜欢 都是一试 不吃不知道 一吃就后悔 后悔我为啥没有早点吃这道菜 并且问了饭店老板 如何烧出地道的臭鳜鱼 方法挺简单 就是普通烧鱼的方法 不过鱼从新鲜的鱼换成了发酵过的臭鳜鱼 从西递宏村回合肥之后 就一直对臭鳜鱼念念不忘 正想尝试自己做的时候呢 又不会腌制鱼 没法自己在家做 后来机缘巧合发现之前微信上加的以后黄山徽州区的 卖黄山烧饼和茶叶的人 在朋友圈里发图 说是也卖臭鳜鱼 果断下单 买了两条 一条先吃 好吃的话 另一条就留着过年吃 不好吃的话 就不要了 收到的鱼是新鲜现杀 抹上调料 其实就是盐和花椒 就快递过来的 反正臭鳜鱼也是需要腌制发酵的 在途的时候就不怕坏了 收到鱼 放了三天 就拿去放冰箱了 后来才知道夏天气温高的时候 基本都要发酵两到三天 动天的话 估计一延长发酵时间 不然就不够臭 第一次做鱼之前 在网上查了各种做法的视频 感觉是不难 一次就成功 我家爱吃鱼的某人 也很喜欢 当然过年的团年饭上 这道菜也就是妥妥的C位啦 可见我和我先生对他的钟爱  后来呢 到三月份鳜鱼正肥美的时候 价格太高 没舍得再买 最近在超市看见了鳜鱼 虽然已经是六十一斤了 还是买了一条 回家自己尝试腌制 毕竟自己腌要便宜一点 应该不会翻车 果然 没有翻车 并且可以复制多次 ～～
recipes.recipeInstructions: 0.腌鱼的步骤：一斤左右的鲜活鳜鱼一条 一定是活的 去鳞去腮去内脏后 直接摸上盐和拍破的干花椒 里外揉搓按摩均匀 盐的量以揉搓按摩之后 鱼的表面有一层薄盐颗粒为准 就是适量的  涂抹好调料的鱼放在保鲜袋里 多裹两次 放入稍大的容器中 表面压重物 密封腌制 夏天两到三天 动天一周左右 正宗臭鳜鱼的腌制是要在木桶里进行的 并且压的是鹅暖石 这个方法不太适合家庭制作 用前面的方式腌制也是可以的 腌好的臭鳜鱼 腮的部位的红色的 ,1.烧制：1、准备烧鱼的辅料：姜蒜切成筷子头大小的颗粒 辣椒切圈 五花肉切片,2.2、腌好的臭鳜鱼洗去盐和花椒 并且用厨房用纸擦干水分 这是为了防止下一步煎鱼的时候炸锅 如果怕鱼太咸 可以加水浸泡再开始,3.3、鱼的身上打上花刀 方便煎熟和入味,4.4、锅中放适量菜籽油 最好是菜籽油 没有的话 换成其他植物油也可以 油热下擦干水分的鱼 一面煎制定型后再翻面 煎至两面金黄后 盛出备用,5.5、锅留底油 下五花肉煸炒出油脂 再下葱姜粒 大部分辣椒圈翻炒 ,6.6、下煎好的鱼 加没过鱼身的热水 ,7.7、调味：锅中加生抽 少许老抽 醋 白糖 盐最后加 因为鱼本身是腌制过的 已经有咸味 可根据个人口味咸淡再加盐,8.8、锅中沸腾之后 烧12分钟 期间可以翻动一到两次 并不断地把料汁浇到鱼身上,9.9、开大火收汁 注意汤汁要自收浓稠 不需要勾芡 起锅前 撒上剩余的青红椒圈就完成啦

recipes.name: 雲南汽鍋雞
recipes.description: 汽鍋中央蒸氣管讓蒸氣凝結成湯，鍋內不加水；雞件與薑蒸出清鮮滋味。普通密封燉盅並不等效。
recipeIngredient: 依器具水位，僅下鍋用 下層水鍋用水

recipeInstructions.name: 檢查汽鍋
recipeInstructions.text: 檢查陶汽鍋無裂紋、中央蒸氣管暢通；確認底座穩合下層水鍋，依器具說明安裝。

recipeInstructions.name: 整理雞件
recipeInstructions.text: 用已完全解凍、一直冷藏≤4°C的雞件；未解凍先另行雪櫃解凍，時間另計。切約4厘米，挑走碎骨及多餘脂肪，以廚房紙吸乾，不沖洗生雞。

recipeInstructions.name: 切薑蔥
recipeInstructions.text: 洗淨薑及全20克蔥；薑切薄片，蔥白切長段、蔥綠切短段，蔥綠蓋好留最後。

recipeInstructions.name: 短醃雞肉
recipeInstructions.text: 雞件拌紹興酒及鹽，放雪櫃10分鐘，同時準備下層熱水。

recipeInstructions.name: 裝入汽鍋
recipeInstructions.text: 汽鍋內鋪薑片與蔥白，放雞件，中央管口周圍留空，不塞滿。

recipeInstructions.name: 鍋內不加水
recipeInstructions.text: 把醃汁倒入汽鍋並蓋原配蓋；內鍋不加水，湯汁由蒸氣凝結形成。

recipeInstructions.name: 下鍋加水
recipeInstructions.text: 下層水鍋在04醃雞時已按器具水位加水煮熱；此時確認大滾。陶汽鍋加熱前溫度及架鍋方法依其原廠說明，勿把雪凍陶器直接架滾水或自行密封接口。內鍋不加水。

recipeInstructions.name: 穩妥架鍋
recipeInstructions.text: 暫關火，戴雙乾厚隔熱手套，把06已蓋好的汽鍋低位穩架匹配下鍋，確認穩固；依器具說明重開火恢復穩定蒸氣，勿封排氣口。

recipeInstructions.name: 持續蒸煮
recipeInstructions.text: 維持穩定蒸氣蒸約90分鐘；避免頻繁開內蓋以保留凝結湯汁。

recipeInstructions.name: 留意下鍋水位
recipeInstructions.text: 每20至30分鐘檢查下鍋水位，依器具安全方式補沸水，勿讓乾燒或冷水濺陶鍋。

recipeInstructions.name: 確認雞熟
recipeInstructions.text: 戴乾厚手套向遠側開蓋避蒸氣，用清潔探針量最厚雞肉中心、避骨達75°C維持30秒。未達標續蒸約10分鐘再測，10分鐘是補煮檢查間隔而非保證熟透；時間按實際增加。

recipeInstructions.name: 調味端鍋
recipeInstructions.text: 加入白胡椒及蔥綠，取走蔥白。戴手套端鍋放隔熱墊，連自然凝結的湯分碗食用。

recipes.description: These lazy cook's pork and cabbage potstickers require NO complicated folding whatsoever. This recipe makes the easiest pork and cabbage potstickers ever!

recipeInstructions.text: Add 2 tablespoons of oil to a non-stick or cast iron pan over medium heat. Place the dumplings in the pan. Once they begin to sizzle, add a quarter cup of water to the pan and cover immediately. Allow the dumplings to cook until the water has evaporated, about 3 minutes. Keep an eye on the pan to make sure nothing is burning, and add a little more water to the pan if necessary. recipeInstructions.name: Make the dough

itemListElement.text: OPTION 1 - USING YOUR HANDS: Combine the flour and salt in a big bowl. Stir to mix well. Slowly drizzle in the hot water while mixing it with a pair of chopsticks (or a fork), until the water is fully absorbed. Slowly drizzle in the cool water, continuing to stir until many dough flakes form. Press the dough together, and try to combine the wet dough with the dry flour. Drizzle in a little extra water if there is any dry flour remaining. Knead until a firm ball is formed, about 5 minutes. Cover and let rest for 20 minutes.

recipeInstructions.name: Cook the pancakes

itemListElement.text: Heat a 9” (23 cm) cast iron pan (or a nonstick skillet) over medium-high heat and add enough oil to fully coat the bottom. Once the oil is hot, add a pancake. Use a pair of chopsticks (or a spatula) to swirl the pancake around to spread the oil and prevent sticking, for a few seconds. Cover the pan and turn the heat down to medium. Let the pancake cook, covered, for 1 minute. Remove the lid and flip the pancake, cover, and cook for another minute. Remove the lid. Use a spatula to press the pancake, to ensure even browning. Continue to cook, flipping regularly, until both sides are crisp and browned, about 3 minutes. Turn to medium-low heat if the pan gets too hot. Transfer the pancake to a cooling rack or a cutting board to cool. Repeat to cook all the pancakes you plan to serve.

recipeInstructions.name: Store and reheat cooked pancakes

itemListElement.text: Place the leftover pancakes in a ziplock bag by stacking them together. Store in the fridge up to 3 days. To reheat, add a pancake to a pan and heat over medium heat, cook, flip occasionally until the pancakes turn warm throughout.
